label: row_0
context: This table compares the relative reactivities of substituted alkenes (dienophiles) in Diels–Alder reactions with cyclopentadiene. Electron-withdrawing substituents such as –CN, –COOR, and –C=O greatly accelerate the reaction by lowering the alkene’s LUMO and stabilizing charge buildup in the polarized transition state. The rates span many orders of magnitude, showing how substituents can dramatically alter diene–dienophile reactivity. Geometric isomers (cis/trans) and modestly activated esters display smaller effects, but the overall trend highlights the dominant role of π-acceptor substituents in promoting Diels–Alder cycloadditions.
